page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is a memory-optimized instance in the EASv4 series, structured to handle large in-memory datasets and dense compute tasks. Driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with two threads per core clocked at 3.525 GHz. The server incorporates 672 GB of system RAM, maintaining a ratio of 7 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 1,443 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present. The x86_64 instruction set supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though newer extensions like AVX-512, AMX, and VNNI are absent.

Performance evaluations demonstrate strong execution across heavily parallelized tasks. The instance achieved top-tier marks in stress-ng multi-core testing (129,815.6) and PassMark CPU encryption (103,059.94), supported by robust Geekbench multi-core and Clang compilation outputs. PassMark memory testing placed in the top tier at 3,036.64, complemented by Redis SET throughput reaching 89.47 million operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1,658.0) and text processing, remain in the middle tier. Furthermore, uncached memory bandwidth registers at average levels (134.24 GB/sec read and 65.08 GB/sec write for 256 MB blocks), showing that memory performance relies considerably on cache locality.

From an efficiency standpoint, the E96as_v4 consolidates high core counts, substantial RAM, and integrated local SSD space into a single deployment, reducing overhead associated with multi-instance clustering. While the lack of hardware accelerators limits specialized deep learning training, its CPU inference rates for small to medium language models remain dependable. The instance delivers a stable hardware foundation for enterprise memory workloads. Best-fit use cases include large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, big data analytics engines, continuous integration build farms, and batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for high-capacity database systems and memory-intensive enterprise computing. Powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.525 GHz. It is provisioned with 672 GB of RAM, offering 7 GB of memory per core, paired with 1,443 GB of bundled local SSD storage. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, but excludes AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Benchmark testing indicates top-tier multi-threaded compute and cryptographic processing alongside top-tier memory metrics. Large-block uncached memory transfers display average throughput, reflecting standard multi-socket scale tradeoffs. The server provides a balanced cost-to-performance profile for resource-dense setups by consolidating large memory footprints onto shared physical sockets. It is best configured for large relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, extensive Clang compilation tasks, and enterprise analytics.
